name: Environment, Carbon Management, and Climate Resilience
summary: Protection tiers, restoration programmes, biodiversity and extinction debt, the chemical regime and legacy pollution, the planetary carbon account, the overturning watch, sea level, and hazard adaptation.

carbonAccount.floorRationale: Below 320 ppm the Concord must stop drawing down. Photosynthesis, yield, and the biosphere it actually has are adapted to the present concentration, and a civilization able to engineer its atmosphere downward would eventually be tempted to keep going. The floor is restraint written as a number.

removalMethods.name: Biological removal
removalMethods.summary: Restoration, soil carbon, and blue carbon. Cheap and reversible — a forest can burn.

removalMethods.name: Direct air capture
removalMethods.summary: Expensive and permanent. A quarter of one percent of planetary generation removes 0.8 Gt a year.

removalMethods.name: Enhanced weathering
removalMethods.summary: Slow and durable; energy cost carried in materials handling.

carbonAccount.portfolioRationale: A removal portfolio with one method is a removal portfolio with one failure mode.

thresholdNotices.name: Threshold notice EY 288
thresholdNotices.summary: Approach to the ceiling after a decade of high cement output.

thresholdNotices.name: Threshold notice EY 341
thresholdNotices.summary: Approach to the floor as removal capacity overshot during low industrial demand.

thresholdNotices.name: Threshold notice EY 396
thresholdNotices.summary: Approach to the floor, same cause.

overturningWatch.canonNote: The Concord cannot detect the trigger condition quickly. If weakening began tomorrow the constitutional emergency would fire around EY 416, by which point the cause would be four years old. The Council of Regions holds that an automatic planetary emergency at 94% confidence is defensible and one at 60% is not. Genuinely unresolved.

seaLevel.structuralAdvantage: Elysium is not one ice sheet away from catastrophe because it does not have an ice sheet of that scale; defences are designed to a defensible worst case rather than an open-ended one.

hazardAdaptation.name: Tropical cyclone
hazardAdaptation.summary: 285 km/h structural design basis, mangrove-analogue and reef buffers, and evacuation infrastructure sized for 90% of exposed population in 36 civil hours.

hazardAdaptation.name: Austral winter storm
hazardAdaptation.summary: Long-duration design; the grid's 14-day islanding rule is largely an austral requirement.

hazardAdaptation.name: Monsoon failure
hazardAdaptation.summary: Food reserves sized against three consecutive warm Amarant phases.

hazardAdaptation.name: Sirocc drought
hazardAdaptation.summary: Fossil-aquifer drawdown ceilings, with desalination and transfer capacity held idle against multi-year events.

hazardAdaptation.name: Alcyon flood
hazardAdaptation.summary: 1-in-500-year design basis, achieved by floodplain reconnection rather than channelisation.

hazardAdaptation.name: Heat extremes
hazardAdaptation.summary: Urban design standards, cool-refuge provision in every Commune, and a statutory work-cessation temperature.

hazardAdaptation.name: Reef bleaching
hazardAdaptation.summary: Thermal-refuge identification and assisted gene flow, triggered at a 1.4 C local anomaly. 2,400 km2 treated; contested and expanding.

protectionTiers.name: Inviolable
protectionTiers.summary: Abyssal plain, Veydran Ice Cap, Verdanne core, Myriad hydrothermal fields. Nothing extractive; research under licence only; reducible only by Tier 1 amendment.

protectionTiers.name: Managed conservation
protectionTiers.summary: Traditional use, low-impact harvest, and tourism under quota.

protectionTiers.name: Connectivity corridor
protectionTiers.summary: Working landscapes managed for passage; farming, forestry, and transport permitted if passage standards are met.

protection.ratchet: Boundaries may be enlarged by ordinary legislation but reduced only by Tier 2 amendment following a published adverse finding, and never for the inviolable tier.
protection.connectivityPrinciple: A reserve a species cannot leave is a large enclosure rather than a habitat. Elysian conservation does not equate protection with absence of people.

programmes.name: Forest and woodland restoration
programmes.summary: Mostly former marginal cultivation returning to temperate broadleaf and taiga.

programmes.name: Wetland and floodplain reconnection
programmes.summary: Alcyon basin and Serapht margins; flood control and carbon in one act.

programmes.name: Grassland and soil restoration
programmes.summary: Meridian Plain margins; soil is accumulating planet-wide.

programmes.name: Post-industrial and mine site restoration
programmes.summary: Funded by restoration bonds posted before extraction begins.

biodiversity.extinctionDebtNote: Published annually, undisputed, and the strongest counter-argument to any account of the Concord as ecologically successful.

deExtinction.objection: Moral hazard: a civilization that believes extinction is reversible will take risks that one believing it permanent will not.
deExtinction.counterArgument: Refusing an available repair in order to preserve a useful fear is itself a moral position.

pollution.darkSkyRationale: Ecological evidence, astronomy, and the cultural place of the aurora, which reaches mid-latitudes on Elysium. Elysians regard a sky you cannot see the aurora from as a defect in a city.

enforcement.commissionRole: measure, publish, and compel a response on breach
enforcement.principalDeterrent: Material passports and open contracting, which make ecological damage visible in records before it becomes visible in ecosystems.

knownWeaknesses.name: Slow overturning detection
knownWeaknesses.summary: Four years to 94% confidence; the constitutional trigger cannot fire faster than the ocean speaks, and the precautionary alternative has been rejected three times.

knownWeaknesses.name: Removal capacity overshoot
knownWeaknesses.summary: Two of three threshold notices concerned the floor; removal infrastructure is easier to build than to modulate.

knownWeaknesses.name: Committed rise is unavoidable
knownWeaknesses.summary: 0.28 m of the recognised commitment remains and no policy affects it.

knownWeaknesses.name: Settlements lost
knownWeaknesses.summary: Eleven Isle settlements gone since EY 300; adaptation has a lower bound and canon names it.

knownWeaknesses.name: Assisted gene flow is unresolved
knownWeaknesses.summary: Permitted, contested, and expanding without an agreed answer to the objection against it.

knownWeaknesses.name: Cement
knownWeaknesses.summary: Residual process emissions are the largest single component of the 1.9 Gt and have resisted forty years of substitution research.

knownWeaknesses.name: Extinction debt
knownWeaknesses.summary: 9,000-14,000 species committed to extinction by damage already done; recovery reaches perhaps a tenth.

knownWeaknesses.name: Legacy persistence
knownWeaknesses.summary: Pre-founding compounds at 34% of peak, clearing around EY 600, with no available acceleration.

knownWeaknesses.name: Prosecution gap
knownWeaknesses.summary: About 40 band 5 ecological convictions a year against harm nobody believes is that small.

knownWeaknesses.name: Paper protection
knownWeaknesses.summary: Protected status is planetary but enforcement is regional; inadequate monitoring found in six Regions with small administrations.

knownWeaknesses.name: Restoration lag
knownWeaknesses.summary: Functional equivalence takes 80-140 years, so present policy is judged on results nobody alive at its adoption will see.

knownWeaknesses.name: The ratchet cuts both ways
knownWeaknesses.summary: Three protected areas are now known to be poorly sited and remain protected anyway.

knownWeaknesses.name: De-extinction unresolved
knownWeaknesses.summary: Licensing is restrictive on a moral-hazard argument that has never been answered, only asserted more loudly by both sides.

knownWeaknesses.name: Nutrient runoff
knownWeaknesses.summary: 8% loop leakage still produces seasonal hypoxia in four Regions.
